newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish T-bill yields seen stable or just up on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Polish T-bill yields seen stable or just up on Monday.

text.p: Polish T-bill yields are likely to stabilise or rise slightly at Monday's 1.1 billion zloty primary tender depending on the treasury's determination to raise funds, analysts said on Friday.

"I expect T-bill yields to stabilise at present levels or slightly rise, depending on how determined the finance ministry is to raise funds," said Krzysztof Kozuchowski, debt dealer at ING Bank in Warsaw.

They expected demand to roughly match the finance ministry's 1.1 billion zloty offer because current yields may be attractive to both domestic and foreign investors after the treasury had significantly raised them over the last months.
Some players, however, were seen bidding for higher yields betting on the finance ministry's small cash reserves.

The treasury increased the maximum yields on all maturities at Tuesday's auction with the benchmark 52-week rising 0.36 point to 21.86 percent. It also raised the maximum yield of the 15 percent two-year bond at the April 2 auction by 0.43 point to 21.44 percent.

The ministry raised the monthly T-bill offer to 5.7 billion zlotys in April from 4.9 billion in March signalling it will need more funds than the net 416 million zlotys in March after it bought back all maturing T-bills that month.
Analysts said the treasury may get some help from the 1996 income tax payments, the bulk of which is due in April.
"Firms will likely postpone tax payments to the very end of April," said Andrzej Hirsz, T-bill dealer at Bank Gdanski SA.
Analysts said that this week's central bank's decision to cap the rise of longer bills' yields at 22.00 percent may shift investor demand to the now more attractive T-bills.
"Investors may now focus on the more attractive T-bills, because they are more liquid, available to clients and may be used as collateral for lombard credit," said ING's Kozuchowski.
Dealers said the caps on NBP-bill yields are likely to stop T-bill yield rises as many traders said the margin of NBP-bills over T-bills should not exceed 0.5 point.
"The market will not expect T-bill yields above the central bank's bills," said an analyst at a foreign company here.
Foreign investors were expected to bid for some 50 million zlotys worth of T-bills, mobilised by an opportunity to buy a high yielding instrument at its possible top.

If it materialises, the zloty could probe strong resistance at three percent from the parity rate next week, but fear of a central bank currency-buying intervention at around that level was likely to keep zloty gains limited.
"Even the foreign entry at the tender is not likely to push the zloty too high because of fear of a central bank intervention," said Wojciech Trzepizur, forex dealer at BRE SA.
The zloty closed the week at 3.03/3.01 percent from the trading band centre, slightly stronger than last Friday's 2.96/2.87 percent. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
